input.summary: Flask app started with debug=True, which enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger (remote code execution if exposed) and leaks stack traces.
input.reasoning: The app.run(debug=True) call is in the `__main__` block, so it only takes effect when the file is run directly and not under a WSGI server such as gunicorn. That reduces the likelihood somewhat. The flag is still hardcoded, so any deployment that starts the file with `python app.py` exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger. The debugger allows arbitrary code execution, though it is PIN-protected. It also leaks source and stack traces. This app also has several other serious flaws: SQL injection, command injection with shell=True, and unsafe yaml.Loader. Those make debug-mode exposure more dangerous, because an attacker who triggers an error gets detailed information to work with. The fix is to drive debug from an environment variable that defaults to off, and to bind to localhost.
